clue.text: … stops to embrace single second lady

definitions.note: a woman of noble rank is called Lady

indicators.note: the stops are said to hug the next pieces, so those letters sit inside

parts.note: bars are things that stop or block
one is single

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a friendly person halts to hug a lone woman, the second lady in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening dots tie the surface to the clue before; they play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A noblewoman holding a peerage title is addressed as Lady, so the title fits the general word.

clue.text: Stroke trophy containing nothing

indicators.note: the trophy holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a cup is a sporting trophy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A golfer's stroke wins a trophy that turns out to be empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a stroke in the sense of a sudden successful move, as in a stroke of genius.

clue.text: Sailor getting stuck into wine produces delay

indicators.note: the sailor is lodged within the wine

parts.note: red is a wine
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor getting into the wine causes the ship to be late.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to slow or hold back progress; both words mean hold up.

clue.text: 'Potter' bilge holds up book

definitions.note: the book of an opera or musical is its text

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom
the two words hold the answer inside their letters

explanation.surface: A dismissive review: the Harry Potter books are rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' marks the letters concealed across 'Potter bilge'; 'up' turns them round, as this is a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The written words of an opera are called its book, a theatrical sense of the word.

clue.text: Military group good to go in Africa perhaps

indicators.note: the letter for good is placed inside the continent

parts.note: Africa is an example of a continent, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Troops are ready to deploy into Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a body of troops forming part of a larger force.

clue.text: Clever commercial rubbish grabs one

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: the rubbish clutches the next piece inside it

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A smart advert grabs one's attention despite being rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone skilful and quick-witted.

clue.text: He plans to destroy and abort use violently

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about violently into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone intends demolition and will use force to halt things.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrecker who deliberately damages equipment or plans is described by this word.

clue.text: River areas possibly indicating danger spots initially

definitions.text: River areas possibly indicating danger spots initially

indicators.note: the opening letters of each word are taken

parts.words: River areas possibly indicating danger spots

explanation.surface: Stretches of river that may warn boaters of hazards.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretches of fast, turbulent water are hazardous parts of a river, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: One disposed of sweetheart's fabulous bride

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
goods disposed of are sold
the heart of the word sweet is E

explanation.surface: Someone sold off a sweetheart's dreamlike bride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is not a lover but the middle letter of 'sweet'; 'fabulous' means legendary, from fable.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend she is betrothed to King Mark but loves Tristan, so she is a bride of fable.

clue.text: Go off to catch male show

indicators.note: the explosion traps the next letter inside

parts.note: to pop is to go off with a bang

explanation.surface: A man is caught when something explodes during a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand ceremonial display; pageantry and show are near synonyms.

clue.text: Desire to Parisian is strange …

indicators.note: a strange arrangement of the letters signals reordering

explanation.surface: Wanting something is alien to a person from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots lead into the next clue's surface; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition or longing for something; both words name a strong wish.

clue.text: … urge of French guy beginning to decline?

parts.note: de is French for of
a guy is a man

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Continuing on, a Frenchman's urge appears to be fading.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge firmly or insist upon something; both verbs express pressing requirement.

clue.text: Sorry self-importance rejected in Capitol after reshuffle

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the rearranged letters
the letters of the word get reshuffled, like a cabinet
rejected means turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: ego is an inflated sense of self-importance

explanation.surface: A politician regrets that arrogance was rebuffed in Washington after a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffle' evokes a cabinet shake-up but signals the anagram; the Capitol is the US Congress building in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling or expressing regret; the adjective sorry and this word share that sense.

clue.text: Greek character, famous, returned and set off

indicators.note: returned means the pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
noted means famous

explanation.surface: A celebrated Greek figure came back home and departed again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ETANOTED around as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to explode it; the phrasal verb means trigger.

clue.text: Ships with reels spinning

indicators.note: spinning round turns the word to face the other way

parts.note: spools are reels for thread or film

explanation.surface: Vessels whose reels are whirling, perhaps fishing boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-masted sailing vessels are a type of ship.

clue.text: Flower originated beneath quiet border

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath puts this piece below the others

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
a rim is a border or edge
to rise is to originate, so rose means originated

explanation.surface: A bloom sprang up below a peaceful flowerbed edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow spring bloom; it is one kind of flower.

clue.text: Look thoroughly? That's an astronomer

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
well can mean thoroughly, as in well shaken

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to peer closely, and is told that is a stargazer's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Percival Lowell was an American astronomer who founded an observatory in Arizona.

clue.text: Cloakroom staff blocking hotel escape

parts.note: cloakroom is a British euphemism for a toilet, a loo

indicators.note: the staff closes round the letter for hotel

parts.note: a pole is a staff
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Washroom attendants obstruct a guest trying to escape the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap in rules that lets someone evade them is a way out, an escape.

clue.text: Stones showing range with group making comeback

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of kitchen range cooker

indicators.note: making a comeback means the word comes back, reversed

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: Gemstones on display with a rock band staging a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy cast-iron cooker common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Banded semi-precious gems of chalcedony are kinds of stone.

clue.text: Head of badger emerging, blinking

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: looming means emerging into view

explanation.surface: A badger peeps out of its sett, blinking in the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blinking' is not eyes but a mild British expletive, like 'flipping'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British intensifiers used in place of a swear word.

clue.text: Hold out underwear that is taken off

indicators.note: the letters for that is are removed, like clothes

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear

explanation.surface: Someone resists while their underwear is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist or stay on, hanging about; holding out has the same sense of lasting.

clue.text: Extraordinarily remote heavenly body

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an extraordinary new way

explanation.surface: A star or planet very far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star burning up in the sky counts as a celestial object.

clue.text: Doctor seeing I'd come around

indicators.note: the letters are turned around into a different order

explanation.surface: A patient tells the GP they will drop by.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a physician or medical student.

clue.text: United get trained differently

indicators.note: the letters are put together differently

explanation.surface: Manchester United players get coached in a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' reads as the football club but is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Combined into one whole; joined together, as united parts are.

clue.text: Small old house in London area

explanation.surface: A tiny period cottage in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A district in London's West End known for nightlife and restaurants.

clue.text: Direct route following sun

indicators.note: the route comes after the letter for sun

parts.note: a way is a route

explanation.surface: A straight path that tracks the sun across the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to influence.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence or govern someone's course of action; to steer or direct them.

clue.text: Row ship across lake

indicators.note: the ship stretches across both sides of the lake

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Someone rows a boat over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a verb about oars but is a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A succession of things one after another, like a line; both mean a sequence.

clue.text: Thus guy embracing one, getting friendly …

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: the rope hugs the next letter inside it

parts.note: a guy is a rope holding a tent or mast, so a cable
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: So this man hugs someone and becomes chummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' is not a man but a guy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone who enjoys company and is affable with others.
